scenes.title: India
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The Maurya Empire (322–185 BCE) unified most of the Indian subcontinent into one state, and was the largest empire to exist in South Asia.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The Chola Empire conquered southern India in the 11th century and were known for their art and architecture.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The British Indian Empire was partitioned in August 1947 into the Dominion of India and Dominion of Pakistan, each gaining its independence.

scenes.caption: Photo 1860 · Agra
scenes.text: The time between the Maurya Empire in the 3rd century BCE and the end of the Gupta Empire in the 6th century CE is referred to as the "Classical" period of India.

scenes.caption: Photo 1862 · Agra
scenes.text: The territory of the empire covered large parts of India from the 1st century BCE onward.

scenes.caption: Photo 1860 · Agra
scenes.text: The Kushan Empire expanded out of what is now Afghanistan into the northwest of the Indian subcontinent under the leadership of their first emperor, Kujula Kadphises, about the middle of the 1st century CE.

scenes.caption: Photo 1862 · Agra
scenes.text: Early medieval India began after the end of the Gupta Empire in the 6th century CE.

scenes.caption: Photo 1864 · Agra
scenes.text: The Chola Empire emerged as a major power during the reign of Raja Raja Chola I and Rajendra Chola I who successfully invaded parts of Southeast Asia and Sri Lanka in the 11th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1862 · Agra
scenes.text: During this period the other major ruling families of the Deccan, the Hoysalas, the Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri, the Kakatiya dynasty and the Southern Kalachuris, were subordinates of the Western Chalukyas and gained their…

scenes.caption: Photo 1862 · Agra
scenes.text: The sultanate was the only Indo-Islamic state to enthrone one of the few female rulers in India, Razia Sultana (r. 1236–1240).

scenes.caption: Photo 1863 · Agra
scenes.text: The empire rose to prominence as a culmination of attempts by the south Indian powers to ward off Islamic invasions by the end of the 13th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1862 · Agra
scenes.text: Lodi rule lasted in Delhi until the defeat of the last sultan, Ibrahim Khan Lodi, in 1526 to the forces of Babur.

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: Hyderabad was founded by the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda in 1591.

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: In 1737, the Marathas defeated a Mughal army in their capital, in the Battle of Delhi.

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 was a large-scale rebellion by soldiers employed by the British East India Company in northern and central India against the company's rule.
